newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Young men take the helm at Nigeria's UBA.
newsitem.headline: Young men take the helm at Nigeria's UBA.

text.p: United Bank for Africa Plc, one of Nigeria's top three, on Friday announced a major management change propelling two highfliers to its helm.
It said the board of directors had unanimously approved the appointment of Abba Kyari, a 44-year-old former newspaper editor as managing director and chief executive officer of the bank.
Kyari, who holds degrees from Britain's Cambridge University and Harvard Business School in the United States replaced Chief Luke Okafor who has headed the bank for five years.
Before his elevation, Kyari was executive director in charge of management services at the bank.
The board also announced that Hakeem Bello-Osagie, a young businessman who has been a major investor in UBA was voted chairman of the board from his former position of vice-chairman.

Bankers said the changes represented a move by UBA to strengthen itself for stiff competition expected in the banking sector following new government regulations requiring banks to shore up their capital bases by 900 percent or be liquidated.
Shares of UBA closed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange on Friday at 7.30 naira from 7.27 on Thursday.

UBA is owned 60 percent by Nigerians and 40 percent by foreigners among them Bank Nationale de Paris Intercontinentale (5.23 percent), Bank Nationale De Paris Plc (UK) (25.47 percent), Bankers International Corp (U.S.) (4.5 percent), Banca Nationale del Lavoro (Italy) (2.4 percent) and Monte dei Paschi di Siena (Italy) 2.4 percent.
A UBA spokesman said the foreign partners had been invited to nominate a vice-chairman.
